The verdict rests on the combined weight of many modest signals. The strongest are POP SUB (+0.016184), XOR ADC (+0.011964), POP LEA (+0.011854), SUB PUSH (+0.011495), ADD POP (+0.010349), CALL PUSH (+0.010224), ADD PUSH (+0.010163) and ADD ADC (+0.010023). The carry-propagating arithmetic pairs XOR ADC, ADD ADC, MOV ADC and ADC SUB are consistent with multi-word arithmetic or mixing/hashing loops, which are typical of mining proof-of-work code. They are not unique to it, though, since big-integer math in benign code produces them too. The most frequent n-grams are stack-management sequences: POP PUSH (0.102679) and PUSH POP (0.089286). They suggest many small functions with heavy register save and restore, or unrolled code. The evidence contains no function names, API calls or strings, so I cannot tie any pattern to a specific mining routine or to network behavior such as pool communication. Several n-grams (ADD POP, CMOVZ MOV, PUSH SUB, XOR CALL) have a frequency of 0.000000 yet carry positive SHAP values. This means the model is also using their absence, or near-absence, as a signal. I therefore treat the classification as statistically strong but not independently corroborated by semantic evidence. Because the model output is unanimous and the arithmetic-heavy patterns fit mining workloads, I assign high-confidence, with the caveat that the evidence is purely statistical.
